newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Police uncover Colombia drug kings' jailbreak bid.
newsitem.headline: Police uncover Colombia drug kings' jailbreak bid.

text.p: Police foiled an apparent jailbreak attempt on Wednesday by Colombia's billionaire cocaine kings, the Rodriguez Orejuela brothers, officials said.

Police intelligence officers, acting on a tip, discovered a false wall and a tunnel leading into a drainage system from the kitchen in the high-security wing of Bogota's La Picota prison where the former chiefs of the Cali drug mob are held.
"Police intelligence services uncovered an escape plan by the two Rodriguez Orejuela brothers," a National Police spokesman said.

Police called in a mechanical digger to excavate an area close to the compound to see where brothers Gilberto and Miguel, who once controlled an estimated 80 percent of the world's cocaine supply, would have emerged from the drains. Prison security was also tightened, the spokesman said.
Rafael Lamo, head of the National Prisons Institute (INPEC), said it was premature to talk of a full-blown escape plan.
"This is a reaction of everybody deprived of their liberty. There are moments of desperation and all inmates have anxiety attacks," Lamo told reporters.
Earlier this week, police cancelled one of the brothers' hospital visits. Both suffer from heart problems and receive regular check-ups at a private clinic in northern Bogota.
The brothers were captured in 1995 and sentenced earlier this year to jail terms that could see them walk free in little more than five years.
Reports of the jailbreak plan coincided with debate in Congress of a government-sponsored bill that would lift Colombia's 6-year-old ban on extradition.

U.S. authorities have been pressing for the Rodriguezes to be extradited to the United States, arguing that the drug lords continue to run their criminal empire from behind bars while they remain in Colombia.
But there has been little indication that the extradition bill would be retroactive.
